hook.text: A single misspelled gene can cause serious disease. Sickle cell anemia changes just one amino acid.

buildup.text: Cystic fibrosis results from a faulty gene that makes mucus too thick to clear from the lungs.

discovery.text: Huntington's disease is caused by a dominant allele—one copy guarantees the condition.

twist.text: Carrying one sickle cell allele actually protects against malaria—a genetic trade-off.

climax.text: Genetic screening can now detect thousands of disorders before symptoms ever appear.

punchline.text: One wrong letter can rewrite a life.

quiz.question: What advantage does carrying one sickle cell allele provide?

details.summary: Genetic disorders are diseases caused by abnormalities in DNA, from single-gene mutations like cystic fibrosis to chromosomal conditions like Down syndrome. Some are inherited from parents while others arise as new mutations during development.
details.whyItMatters: Genetic disorders affect millions of people worldwide. Understanding their molecular basis enables genetic testing, carrier screening, prenatal diagnosis, and increasingly, targeted therapies and gene-based cures.
takeaways: Single-gene disorders follow predictable inheritance patterns
Chromosomal disorders involve changes to whole chromosome structure or number
Multifactorial disorders arise from gene-environment interactions

faq.question: What are the most common genetic disorders?
faq.answer: Sickle cell disease, cystic fibrosis, thalassemia, and Huntington's disease are among the most well-known single-gene disorders. Down syndrome is the most common chromosomal disorder. Heart disease and diabetes involve multiple genes and environment.

faq.question: Can genetic disorders be prevented?
faq.answer: Carrier screening and genetic counseling help at-risk couples understand their chances. Preimplantation genetic testing during IVF can select unaffected embryos. Gene therapy and CRISPR are beginning to offer cures for some conditions.
